LANDED 81ec3f25d (2026-09-02; refuter FIX-THEN-MERGE -> MERGE with the
movement classification corrected + two doc precisions, all folded;
DIRECTION CHANGE VALIDATED at full strength -- gate lib 1571/0/5, cli
24/0, matrix 449/0/9).

BOTH AUTHORIZED DIRECTIONS REFUTED, twice (builder by probe, refuter by
independent re-derivation): (a) cross-key subsumption -- the three
same-function keys {[],[]}/{[],[int]}/{[],[int]}|{[int],[]} are a
TRUNCATED ASCENT LADDER, not redundant siblings; dedup deletes two and
still leaves {[int],[int]} (the fold's actual product) uncovered.
(b) one-return-contract for members -- the wrapper that breaks under
the 138 flip (split_while, construction 27) has AGREEING member
return layouts; the real disagreement lives on take_while =
fz-kdt.148, latent and separate.

THE LANDED LAW (a deletion, judged 'the opposite of a patch'):
resolve_closure_call stops running observed arguments through
refine_contract_inputs against the closure clause's arrow parameters
-- those parameters are EVIDENCE (the surface the lambda has been
analyzed at), not a contract; intersecting clamped every call back
onto the seed specialization (probe: three distinct observed
accumulators all refined to [int,{[],[]}]), truncating the
accumulator's ascent one rung short and leaving the fold's product
with no member that named it. Declared @spec contracts still refine
in apply_function_contract (a declared ARROW's domain no longer
narrows f.(x) -- measured behaviour-neutral; doc'd). The
argument-side rule is UNCONDITIONAL -- stronger than
refine_observed_return's strict-subtype refusal, which the law
implies (doc'd).

RESULTS (every number refuter-re-derived): the ENTIRE 268-escape
surface-membership census EMPTIES -- 0 corpus-wide at settled and
under every stress setting; the one-line revert restores exactly
16/16/4/16/106/106/4 (the fix is the sole cause). fz-kdt.147 RETIRED
(the order never decided whether a covering member existed).
fz-kdt.138 UNBLOCKED (flip probe: expected output on all three
doors, zero corpus movers under the flip -- but its F2 acceptance
signal is VACUOUS, already green at head AND base; re-scoped on the
ticket). Movement: 12 canon movers = 7 fewer execs (00420 twins
215->196: three seed rungs collapse into the grown accumulator) + 3
more (the never-minted rung, per-key justified incl. map_enumerable's
honest int|float accumulator base left uncovered) + 2 flat with
WIDER covering keys (widening-to-covering IS the mechanism);
corpus-wide 5018->4982 executables, any-keys 145->146; behaviour
0 movers over 585x2 doors + all stress settings; lenses FIFO==LIFO,
schedule census still exactly 3 at identical line counts; eval rise
742->880 machine-held legitimate (uncaused empty, zero-change flat
at 9, corpus wall clock 7362->7351ms, take_drop 406->381ms).
Related: fz-kdt.76's ascent-truncation record was this defect seen
from the other side. Bycatch: 00424_protocol_no_impl's pre-existing
artifact.rs:155 panic is unowned -> fz-kdt.149.

comments.text:
CONFIRMED and QUANTIFIED from fz-kdt.119's landing (4ca1dc7e7), which shipped the carve-out this ticket blocks.

The carve-out is one function, read by the lattice and by all three lowerings alike: runtime_type_predicate::lowering_tests_position -- a tuple position whose sub-predicate can admit a LIST is not tested at all. Testing only its non-list axes would make the test STRICTER than the type (a position's question is a disjunction; dropping a disjunct rejects values the arm's surface names), so the choice was to decide the list axis there or be blind, and deciding it is what reaches this ticket's dead-and-broken member. Blind counts as overlapping AND as erasing, so no seat can claim it as separation.

The new tripwire measures the cost of staying blind. FZ_STRESS_ASSERT_SURFACE_MEMBERSHIP=1 over the corpus at head reports 106 escapes on 00420_enum_take_drop_split and 106 on behavior/enum_take_drop_split (the same program by two paths) -- 212 of the baseline's 268, and a sampled line shows exactly the shape this ticket names: lists {Empty} at position 0 of a 2-tuple, taking a cons.

So this ticket is the single largest entry in the tripwire baseline, and closing it is what lets fz-kdt.138 flip lowering_tests_position to true and take those 212 with it.

fz-kdt.141's wrapper-permutation stress: THE MEASURED VERDICT IS A NEGATIVE, honestly reported.

The wrapper half now exists (FZ_STRESS_PERMUTE_DISPATCH=wrappers:<seed> permutes flow.first_class_edges in jobs/runtime_demand.rs, upstream of members AND selection, so fz-kdt.108's body_id weld holds). It DOES reach this ticket's pair: the backend canon of enum_take_drop_split moves 972 lines under wrappers:1, and the moved lines are the selection plan's own test nodes swapping -- 'n2 test s1 type(fp[T] {list(int), int})' becomes 'n2 test s1 type(fp[T] {empty_list(), int})'. So the perturbation lands exactly on the {empty_list(), int} / {list(int), int} pair this ticket names.

IT DOES NOT PRODUCE 'backend callable construction 27 matched no member', on any door, at any seed. stdout and exit are identical across the whole 584-fixture corpus, interp and JIT, and across the census fixtures on AOT.

WHY, and it sharpens this ticket rather than weakening it: reordering does not make the dead member LIVE ALONGSIDE its sibling, it makes it live INSTEAD of it. The tuple test is blind at the list position, so whichever member is first takes every value -- one member is always dead. Each member is self-consistent when it takes everything (its own boundary marshals its own return form), so no caller ever sees two disagreeing return contracts. The break this ticket describes needs the two members reached by DIFFERENT values, which is exactly what fz-kdt.138's exact test does and what no ordering can do. So an order stress can never catch this class, and fz-kdt.136's expectation ('expected immediate catch: the take_drop blocker') is refuted by measurement.

WHAT THE WRAPPER STRESS DID CATCH is bigger and is filed as fz-kdt.147: the whole 268-escape FZ_STRESS_ASSERT_SURFACE_MEMBERSHIP baseline is wrapper-order-decided (268 settled -> 68 at wrappers:1 -> 20 at wrappers:6, five of seven fixtures to zero, this fixture 106 -> 34 -> 10), and arm-order seeds move it by ZERO. The settled order is the worst of the legal orders. This ticket owns the largest entry in that baseline, so 147 is its immediate neighbour.

FIXED at c31b309d0 -- and the ticket's own two fix directions were both REFUTED by measurement. Reporting the remap honestly.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY WAS. Not (a) cross-key subsumption and not (b) disagreeing return contracts. At 8002889ff the wrapper that breaks under the 138 flip is construction identity 27, the split_while/split_with reducer, and its three members' return layouts already AGREE (all ShapeId(91) / [RawAtom, ValueRef, ValueRef]) -- so (b) has nothing to repair there. The break is COVERAGE: members are keyed {[], []}, {[], [int]} and {[], [int]} | {[int], []}, the fold delivers {[int], [int]}, and no member names it. Direction (a) would have deleted two of three members and still not covered it.

ROOT CAUSE, proven with a probe on resolve_closure_call. A closure clause's arrow parameters are EVIDENCE -- the surface that lambda has been analyzed at -- not a contract. refine_contract_inputs INTERSECTED every observed argument with them. The reducer is minted beside the fold's initial accumulator {[], []} and keeps that arrow, so the probe shows the observed argument climbing (int, {[], []}) -> (int, {[], [int]}) -> (int, {[], [int]} | {[int], []}) against a clause_args frozen at (int, {[], []}), refined back to (int, {[], []}) every time. The callee activation is therefore always the initial specialization, its return {:cont, {[], [int]} | {[int], []}} is the only return that ever feeds the loop, the ascent stops one rung short, and {[int], [int]} gets no specialization, no member, nowhere to belong. Enum.split_pair_finish was keyed on {[], [int]} | {[int], []} -- a pair it never receives. refine_observed_return already refuses the mirror narrowing on the return side; the argument side did not.

THE FIX is one line plus its prose: the argument decides, unnarrowed. Declared @spec contracts still refine, in apply_function_contract, where the surface is also enforced.

WHAT IT BOUGHT. The whole 268-escape FZ_STRESS_ASSERT_SURFACE_MEMBERSHIP census -> 0, all seven fixtures, and 0 under wrappers:1/wrappers:6/arms:reverse/arms:1/arms:6 as well. Every escape in that census was this one defect. fz-kdt.138's flip, applied as a probe and reverted, takes take_drop and 00420 from 'matched no member' (interp) / function_clause fault trap (JIT, AOT) to the expected output on all three doors.

RED FIRST: compiler2_no_value_reaches_a_construction_member_that_never_named_it, the shell census driven in process, red at base with exactly 16/16/4/16/106/106/4 = 268.

MOVEMENT: 12 canon movers of 457 comparable, 0 behaviour movers over 585 fixtures. 00420 emits 215 -> 196 executables (three partial reducer rungs collapse into one grown accumulator); three fixtures gain the rung that was never minted. Ratchets re-pinned with cause: inventory 215 -> 196; take_drop Activation claims 211 -> 250, AnalyzeActivation 742 -> 880, zero-change FLAT at 9, wall clock 0.410s -> 0.385s.

Gates: lib 1571/0/5, cli 24/0, matrix --test-threads=1 449/0/9, clippy -D warnings, fmt, release.

title: A closure clause's arrow parameters are evidence, not a contract: the resolution point stops clamping calls onto the seed specialization
